title: Spills and Accidents
short: Apologize briefly, help clean up, offer to pay for damage, and move on; as a host, reassure the guest and make light of it.
trouble: Learners apologize over and over all evening, which keeps the attention on the accident. One sincere apology and a fix is enough.

blocks.html: Accidents happen at every table: a knocked glass, a dropped plate, a stain on a host's rug. Like any small slip in etiquette, the goal is to put everyone back at ease quickly.
Apologize briefly, help clean up, offer to pay for any damage, and move on. As a host, reassure the guest and make light of it.

After a spill, everyone feels a moment of tension, and the guest who caused it feels worst. One sincere apology and quick help fix the mess and settle the moment. Apologizing again and again keeps everyone's attention on the accident and forces others to keep reassuring. A host who laughs it off tells the guest that they matter more than the rug.

blocks.title: Red sauce on the tablecloth
blocks.q: At a dinner party, Mia drips red sauce on Rosa's white tablecloth. What should she do?
steps: Apologize once: "I'm so sorry about your tablecloth."
Help blot it with a napkin if the host wants help.
Offer to pay for cleaning, then rejoin the conversation.
blocks.a: Apologize once, help, offer to pay, and move on.

blocks.title: The host's side
blocks.q: A guest breaks one of Kofi's glasses. What should Kofi do?
steps: Reassure the guest: "Please don't worry. Are you all right?"
Clean it up quickly himself, keeping guests clear of the broken glass.
Change the subject and never bring it up again.
blocks.a: Reassure the guest and make light of it.
